cost: For B input bytes, R rows and L extracted links: parsing/normalization O(B), sort O(P log P), hash joins expected O(R), AIM/link dedup can be quadratic. File and DNS/network latencies unbounded; cache bodies and rows use O(B+R) storage.
description: fetch caches raw OpenStax/AIM/OTL pages; build constructs Rows in OpenStax, sorted OTL subject/page, AIM order, then derives license/topic/PDF and cross-catalog joins. find_pdfs caches pages, skips prohibited candidates, ranks links and merges previous output rows.
forward: fetch caches raw OpenStax/AIM/OTL pages; build constructs Rows in OpenStax, sorted OTL subject/page, AIM order, then derives license/topic/PDF and cross-catalog joins. find_pdfs caches pages, skips prohibited candidates, ranks links and merges previous output rows.
inverse: Inner exclusions: explicit closed license conflict forces Other, so the same row cannot remain allowed; NC/ND/unknown variants never satisfy BookLicense::allowed. Cached page save does not make a request. This does not imply build is network-free: GitHub DNS checks remain.

For a TSV row y, compatible raw catalog rows are all schema inputs whose normalized title/surname, precedence-selected license and PDF projections produce y. Entity decoding, whitespace collapse and dropped fields create many antecedents; cross-catalog provenance cannot be uniquely reconstructed from the row alone.
limitations: No network/DNS/download, real catalog/corpus/model/teacher or database execution. Effect paths are source-derived; finite helper tests are not universal verification. No executable percentage surrogate or speed claim; future caps require metric/domain/reference and remain 1/2/5/10%.
state: OTL repeated integer ids retain the first sorted-page occurrence (missing ids share -1). Title plus surname keys are normalization classes, not identities. License overrides precede PDF substitution, so PDF substitution is not a second license reconciliation pass. Output order follows row construction; HashMap count ties need not print stably.
